svg.aria-label: VHTR scale cascade: site to TRISO coating layer
svg.title: VHTR — The Scale Cascade
svg.text: — a 950 °C VHTR resolved across six decades
Every stage is the highlighted region of the one before it. Follow the amber wedges: 30 m of plot down to a 35 µm silicon-carbide shell — and the path the heat takes through all of it.

g.text: warm air out — no plume, no steam
Scale by replication, not by size
One helium loop, six states, no water
20 m of chimney height comes free with the
excavation — natural draught, no fan, no valve.
6.5 MW of decay heat raises it just 100 °C in 1.5 hours.
The manufacturing bet: a printed gyroid, not a drilled hole
≈ 20 gyroid unit cells across the block
network cannot be drilled. That is the point.
A triply periodic minimal surface splits the
one helium, one graphite — with zero mean
curvature everywhere. No corners, no flow
separation, maximum area per unit volume.
That surplus is what buys a 4 MPa primary
Particles drawn at true relative size: each
speck is a 0.93 mm coated pressure vessel.
0.14 g of ²³⁵U per compact, split
own pressure vessel, so a failure
is one particle — never the core.
Each step is a thermal resistance:
LAYER STACK — TRUE PROPORTION, 0 → 465 µm RADIUS
35 µm of CVD β-SiC, intact to 1,600 °C
360 °C of headroom — with no operator action, ever.
